issue.body:
core; ref #30979

1. avoid calling `grpc_dump_slice` if the log level is too low (and the result will be ignored)
2. use `GRPC_TRACE_FLAG_ENABLED(x)` over `x.enabled()` in the touched code

body:
Is there any chance you can port this fix also to Grpc.Core package where this issue was found?
The impact of these traces is significant, and the fix is pretty simple and has a very low risk.
Here is a simple benchmark test that we ran, comparing WCF vs Grpc.Core, by running 19 different queries sequentially, with a parallelism of 50 users (which is fairly low based on the size of the cluster and the SKU type) where in 3 different queries we can see a significant degradation when using Grpc.Core:

![GrpcCore_Vs_WCF](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8223197/195081232-2b694f8b-701b-4ae3-9982-0ec25cc05e85.png)

When running PerfView in the background, we can see that around 19% of the CPU is busy just on dump_out_append (or practically busy in parameters calculations which are passed to tracing methods that aren't going to trace anything eventually):

![dump_out_append](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8223197/195082359-e6f7f166-7492-41b2-9fe9-609fa4efbf26.png)

When focusing on inclusive CPU time, we see that 51% of the CPU is busy at grpc_csharp_ext.x64!grpc_core::ExecCtx::Flush.
The cost of this Flush method is split to two methods, where each one of these methods eventually calls two other methods: hexdump and asciidump:

![Flush1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8223197/195082608-37bd3411-314f-485b-8da9-1580c3303155.png)

![Flush2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8223197/195082714-3a6eaf97-290c-456e-b697-efb2cbccf1f9.png)

![Flush3](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8223197/195082723-c51b0fa1-7b30-42d7-a046-b98c3e2042df.png)
@jtattermusch would be able to help you with that

> @jtattermusch would be able to help you with that

It seems that to get the fix available in Grpc.Core (which is in maintenance mode btw), it would be enough to simply backport the fix (https://github.com/grpc/grpc/pull/31098) to the v1.46.x branch (which is the LTS branch for Grpc C# 2.46.x).
So once https://github.com/grpc/grpc/pull/31098 is merged, I'd be happy to accept a backport PR.
